les: Bo of onder die ewenaar: waar Suid-Afrika lê
kaps_punt: Lengte- en breedtegraad (grade): Konsep van halfronde; Noordelike en Suidelike halfronde - geskei deur die ewenaar; Oostelike en Westelike halfronde - geskei deur die Greenwich Meridiaan en 180 grade lengtelyn; Enige plek op die aardbol is in twee halfronde - noord of suid en oos of wes; Ligging van Suid-Afrika in Suidelike-en Oostelike-halfronde

items.bewering: Sny 'n lemoen middeldeur en jy hou twee gelyke helftes in jou hande. Die aarde is ook 'n bal wat 'n mens in gedagte so kan deursny. Die snit moet reg deur die middel van die bal loop. Ons noem elke sulke helfte van die aarde 'n halfrond.
items.blok: Die aarde in twee gelyke helftes
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemispheres_of_Earth): 'any division of the globe into two equal halves (hemispheres)'. Wikipedia 'Equator' and '180th meridian': the equator is a great circle, and the prime meridian plus the 180th meridian form a great circle/ellipse that halves the Earth. Mapping test: a cut through the centre of a ball gives equal halves, and a cut off-centre gives unequal pieces. The lesson insists on 'reg deur die middel', so the mapping matches the real definition (a plane through the centre, i.e. a great circle). A learner reasoning further from it lands on the truth, not a misconception.

items.bewering: Die aarde is ook 'n bal
items.blok: Die aarde in twee gelyke helftes
items.bron: Ritter, The Physical Environment, 'Size and Shape' (geo.libretexts.org) and CSULB Geography 140 lecture notes: the Earth is an oblate spheroid, equatorial radius 6 378 km against polar radius 6 357 km, flattening about 1/298. At Grade 6 'bal' is a fair simplification, and the deviation does not affect any hemisphere claim in the lesson (Wikipedia notes that on a spheroid the prime meridian with the antimeridian strictly forms a 'great ellipse').

items.bewering: Lyne op 'n aardbol wys die helftes sonder dat iemand iets sny.
items.blok: Die aarde in twee gelyke helftes
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Prime Meridian' encyclopedic entry (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/prime-meridian/): the equator and the prime meridian with the International Date Line are reference lines dividing the globe into hemispheres. Globes conventionally draw them.

items.bewering: Die ewenaar loop soos 'n gordel om die middel van die aarde.
items.blok: Die ewenaar skei noord van suid
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Equator' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equator): a circle of latitude 'equidistant from its poles', 'the only line of latitude which is also a great circle'. Mapping test: a belt goes all the way round at the middle, i.e. a closed loop halfway between top and bottom. That matches a full circle equidistant from both poles. It also matches the Earth bulging at the equator (the widest girth). No misleading inference found.

items.bewering: Hierdie een lyn sny die hele aarde in twee halfronde. Die helfte noord van die ewenaar is die Noordelike Halfrond. Die helfte suid daarvan is die Suidelike Halfrond.
items.blok: Die ewenaar skei noord van suid
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Equator': the equator 'divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres'. Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth': Northern Hemisphere is 'the half that lies north of the Equator', Southern 'the half that lies south of the Equator'.

items.bewering: Die ewenaar is 'n volle sirkel wat om die hele aarde loop.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Equator': a circle of latitude and a great circle.

items.bewering: Die Greenwich Meridiaan loop nie 'n volle sirkel om die aarde nie. Dit loop net van die Noordpool tot die Suidpool oor een kant van die aarde.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Prime meridian' and the meridian definition quoted in search (thewisepilot.com 'Useful Definitions', consistent with Wikipedia): a meridian is 'the half of an imaginary polar great circle ... terminated by the North Pole and the South Pole'. National Geographic Education, 'Prime Meridian': the prime meridian is the 0° line through Greenwich, fixed by international agreement. (Modern GPS 0° lies about 102 m east of the historic Greenwich line, which does not affect this lesson.)

items.bewering: Reg oorkant hom loop die lengtelyn van 180 grade oor die ander kant. Die twee lyne maak saam een volle sirkel om die aarde.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Wikipedia '180th meridian' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/180th_meridian): 'the meridian 180° both east and west of the prime meridian', and together with it forms 'a great ellipse that divides the planet' into Eastern and Western Hemispheres. National Geographic Education, 'Prime Meridian': the prime meridian and the date line 'form a circle' splitting the Earth into Eastern and Western hemispheres.

items.bewering: Die Oostelike Halfrond lê oos van die Greenwich Meridiaan tot by die lengtelyn van 180 grade.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Eastern Hemisphere' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Hemisphere): 'the half of the planet Earth which is east of the prime meridian' and west of the antimeridian. National Geographic Education: east of the prime meridian and west of the International Date Line. Alternative convention, not a contradiction: Britannica (britannica.com/print/article/1108056, via search summary) gives 20°W and 160°E as the 'usual' cartographic boundaries and names the 0°/180° split as the stricter definition 'some geographers' use. Wikipedia says 20°W/160°E is 'sometimes used outside of matters of physics and navigation'. The lesson uses the 0°/180° definition, which is the one its own CAPS point names. It is correct under that definition.

items.bewering: Die Westelike Halfrond lê wes van die Greenwich Meridiaan tot by daardie selfde lyn.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth' and '180th meridian'. Britannica 'Western Hemisphere' (britannica.com/print/article/1108059, via search summary) gives the prime-meridian-to-180th-meridian definition as the strict alternative to 20°W/160°E. Set test with the preceding sentence: the two definitions together cover the whole globe without overlap, and both stop at the same two lines.

items.bewering: Hierdie verdeling vat dus twee lyne en nie net een nie.
items.blok: Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne
items.bron: Follows from the two items above (Wikipedia '180th meridian': the prime meridian and the 180th meridian together divide East from West). Each meridian is a half-circle, so one alone does not enclose a hemisphere.

items.bewering: Elke plek wat nie op 'n grenslyn lê nie, lê in twee halfronde tegelyk. Die een halfrond lê noord of suid van die ewenaar. Die ander een lê oos of wes van die Greenwich Meridiaan, tot by die lengtelyn van 180 grade.
items.blok: Elke plek lê in twee halfronde, en die lyne is die grense
items.bron: Derived from the definitions in Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth', 'Eastern Hemisphere' and '180th meridian'. North and South do not overlap, and neither do East and West. So a point on none of the three lines lies in exactly one of each, i.e. two at once. The qualifier is needed and correctly placed. Points on the lines (including both poles, which lie on every meridian) are excluded, and Wikipedia does not assign boundary points to either half. Set test: a country crossed by a line (e.g. Kenya, Brazil on the equator; Russia and Fiji on the 180° line; the UK on the prime meridian) lies 'op 'n grenslyn' and so falls outside the rule. This agrees with list step 3. The rule never claims that such a country lies in only two hemispheres.

items.bewering: Die lyne self is die grense.
items.blok: Elke plek lê in twee halfronde, en die lyne is die grense
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth' and '180th meridian': the equator divides N/S, and the prime meridian with the 180th meridian divides E/W.

items.bewering: Die ewenaar loop oor die middel van Afrika.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Britannica 'Africa' (britannica.com/place/Africa, via search summary): the equator cuts the continent 'almost equally in two', though because of the western bulge the greater part of the territory lies north of it. Wikipedia 'Extreme points of Africa' and 'Ras ben Sakka': the mainland runs from about 37°20'N (Tunisia) to 34°51'S (Cape Agulhas), so the equator sits near the north-south midpoint. Wikipedia 'Equator': it crosses Sao Tome and Principe, Gabon, Republic of the Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Somalia. Note for a person, not a fault: 'middel' holds for north-south extent. By land area about two-thirds of Africa lies north (WorldAtlas, and Britannica as above), and the lesson does not claim otherwise.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika lê ver suid daarvan aan die suidpunt van die kontinent.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Extreme points of Africa': Cape Agulhas, South Africa (34°51'15"S) is the southernmost point of mainland Africa. Wikipedia 'Extreme points of South Africa': the northernmost point of the country is Over Vlakte farm, Limpopo, 22°7'40"S. So even the north of the country is about 22° (roughly 2 400 km) south of the equator, and 'ver suid' holds. The superlative is established.

items.bewering: Elke deel van die land lê dus suid van die ewenaar.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Extreme points of South Africa': northernmost point 22°7'40"S. Wikipedia 'Prince Edward Islands' and Ramsar site record 1688 (rsis.ramsar.org/ris/1688): the South African-administered Prince Edward Islands lie at about 46°38'-46°58'S. Every part of South African territory, islands included, is south of the equator.

items.bewering: Die Greenwich Meridiaan loop oor die weste van Afrika.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: WorldAtlas 'Countries on the Prime Meridian' and Wikipedia 'Prime meridian': in Africa it crosses Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo and Ghana. Wikipedia 'Extreme points of Africa': the mainland runs from 17°33'W (Senegal) to 51°27'E (Somalia). The meridian lies about 17.5° from the western tip of a ~69° span, i.e. in the western part of the continent.

items.bewering: Die land lê heeltemal oos van die Greenwich Meridiaan.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Extreme points of South Africa': westernmost point is the Orange River mouth near Alexander Bay, 16°27'E. Easternmost is Prince Edward Island at 38°0'5"E (mainland: near Kosi Bay, 32°53'30"E). Every part of South African territory, islands included, lies between about 16°E and 38°E. None of it is west of 0°.

items.bewering: Daarom lê Suid-Afrika in die Suidelike Halfrond en die Oostelike Halfrond.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Follows from the two extreme-point items above (Wikipedia 'Extreme points of South Africa': 22°S-47°S, 16°E-38°E) under the 0°/180° definitions (Wikipedia 'Eastern Hemisphere'). It also holds under Britannica's alternative 20°W/160°E convention, so no convention changes this answer.

items.bewering: Dit lê wel wes van die lengtelyn van 180 grade, maar oos en wes word van die Greenwich Meridiaan af gesê.
items.blok: Waar Suid-Afrika lê
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth' and 'Eastern Hemisphere': the Eastern Hemisphere lies 'west of the 180th meridian'. National Geographic Education: 'west of the International Date Line'. So calling South Africa (16°-38°E) west of the 180° line follows standard usage. Longitude east and west is measured from the prime meridian (National Geographic Education, 'Prime Meridian': 'the reference point for measuring distance east and west'). Direction and consistency test: under the lesson's own definitions every Eastern-Hemisphere place is west of the 180° line, so this sentence agrees with the block 'Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne'. The 'maar' stops a learner from reading 'west of 180°' as 'Western Hemisphere'.

items.bewering: Kyk eers of die land noord of suid van die ewenaar lê. / Kyk dan of dit oos of wes van die Greenwich Meridiaan lê, tot by die lengtelyn van 180 grade. / Lê die land heeltemal aan een kant van elke lyn, dan gee hierdie twee stappe sy twee halfronde.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n land se twee halfronde kry
items.bron: Tested as a set against the definitions (Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth', 'Eastern Hemisphere', '180th meridian') and real countries. South Africa: step 1 south (22°-47°S), step 2 east and short of 180° (16°-38°E), step 3 wholly on one side of all three lines, so Southern + Eastern. This is correct and matches 'Waar Suid-Afrika lê'. Japan (about 123°-154°E, northern): Northern + Eastern, correct. 'Tot by 180' is load-bearing: without it a learner could also reach Japan by going west from Greenwich. Russia (crossed by the 180° line per Wikipedia '180th meridian'), Fiji, Kenya/Brazil (equator), the UK (prime meridian): each fails step 3's 'heeltemal ... elke lyn' condition, so the steps correctly do not give exactly two hemispheres. 'Elke lyn' covers the 180° line as well, which is right for Russia. No case found where the steps give an answer different from the definitions, from 'Elke plek lê in twee halfronde' or from 'Waar Suid-Afrika lê'.

items.bewering: halfrond: Een van die twee gelyke helftes van die aarde. 'n Volle sirkel wat reg om die aarde loop en deur sy middel sny, maak die twee helftes. Die ewenaar is op sy eie so 'n sirkel. Die sirkel wat oos van wes skei, bestaan uit twee lyne: die Greenwich Meridiaan en die lengtelyn van 180 grade.
items.blok: halfrond
items.bron: Read alone, with the rest of the lesson removed. Wikipedia 'Hemispheres of Earth': a hemisphere is a division of the globe into two equal halves. Wikipedia 'Equator': the equator is a great circle. Wikipedia '180th meridian': the prime meridian and the 180th meridian together form the great circle (great ellipse on a spheroid) that divides East from West. Every sentence is true on its own, and 'deur sy middel sny' correctly restricts the circle to a great circle. Set test with blocks 'Die ewenaar skei noord van suid' and 'Die ooste en die weste vat twee lyne': the entry agrees with them. Equator is one line, the E/W circle is two lines, and nothing in the entry gives a different rule.

opsomming: All 22 claims are confirmed and no rule in the lesson gives a different hemisphere answer from another, including for real countries that straddle a line; a person should only know that Britannica also records a cartographic 20°W/160°E east-west convention, which does not affect this lesson because it uses the 0°/180° definition its CAPS point names and South Africa is Southern and Eastern under both.
